children: ) Pacific Power utility asked California regulators Friday to approve a 57% rate increase that would hike the typical residential electricity bill by $120/month.
The increase would boost the utility's base revenue by $103M/year and reflects capital spending already under way to safeguard the grid.

Pacific Power's equipment has allegedly been tied to two blazes in California: the 2020 Slater Fire that burned more than 150K and killed two people and the 2022 McKinney Fire that burned 60K acres and killed four people.
that the company is swapping wooden power poles for steel and fiberglass structures and replacing hundreds of miles of bare wire with insulated, fire-resistant conductor.

Beyond the rate case, Pacific Power faces $637M in liability claims and legal expenses stemming from the 2020 and 2022 fires, and it is asking regulators to let it recover $340.5M of that sum from customers.

Pacific Power's Northern California territory sweeps across 11,292 square miles from the coast to the Nevada border, serving ~46K customers—about four customers per square mile; the utility also operates in Oregon, where it has ~630K customers.

title: Berkshire Hathaway utility asks California regulators for 57% rate increase
